Timex's Marlin Neo Classic Chronograph takes its cue from the mid-century Marlin, a line that debuted in the 1950s and became a centerpiece of Timex's collection in the 1960s. The 40mm case is brushed stainless steel with curved pushers and a polished top ring, and the cream dial pairs metallic blue numerals and hands with a tachymeter scale for reading average speed. The 20mm stainless steel bracelet fastens with a butterfly clasp that folds shut from both sides, and the watch is water resistant to 164 feet, enough for light swimming.

entry.content:
Sea salt meets three of the world's hottest peppers for a seasoning that brings heat to every bite. Firecracker Farm's Three Kings Hot Salt infuses sea salt with Carolina Reaper, Trinidad Scorpion, and Ghost pepper extract through a proprietary process of the family's own invention, with no vinegar, no sugar, and no preservatives. Use it where you'd reach for the hot sauce: because it's dry, the heat spreads evenly across the plate instead of landing in one bite, and the dose is entirely yours. The stainless steel push grinder dispenses about 33mg per one-handed press, so a single press adds big flavor with just a whisper of warmth, and a few more presses bring serious fire. It's as satisfying to use as it is to taste. Press it over eggs and breakfast bowls, on-the-go sandwiches, creamy Italian pasta, even sweet guava desserts. It arrives as something special and becomes the thing you reach for at every meal.

A hand-painted two-tone pearl livery takes its colors from Martin's crash helmet, one-off forged magnesium wheels nod to the Brabham he drove in Formula 1, and the dash carries a signature quote: "The most important bit of the car is the nut holding the steering wheel." An air-cooled, twin-turbo 4.0-liter flat-six makes 860 horsepower through a six-speed manual in a car that weighs about 2,700 pounds. Each of the five buyers also gets an F1-homologated Bell helmet painted to match and signed by Martin.

entry.title: Basquiat Untitled 'Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads' Painting
entry.summary: Jean-Michel Basquiat's Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads) is a bright orange, 84-inch-square canvas from 1983 that riffs on the grotesque heads of Leonardo da Vinci. Basquiat reproduces all five heads from a drawing Leonardo made around 1493, but where Leonardo gave
entry.content:
Jean-Michel Basquiat's Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads) is a bright orange, 84-inch-square canvas from 1983 that riffs on the grotesque heads of Leonardo da Vinci. Basquiat reproduces all five heads from a drawing Leonardo made around 1493, but where Leonardo gave his caricatures bodies, Basquiat reduces them to a slimy grin, an ape-like grimace and a mouth in full howl, and in one corner a pink patch reads "ALTER EGO," a reference to himself. "We see him improvising off the great Master," says Ana Maria Celis, the auction house's head of post-war and contemporary art. The painting has been out of public view in a private European collection for more than two decades and is now up for auction.

entry.content:
McLaren Racing is selling five of the Formula One cars in its Heritage Collection because, as CEO Zak Brown puts it, "These cars were built to be driven and raced, and we want to see them being used and enjoyed." The oldest are a pair of 1991 MP4/6As, chassis 4 and 7, from the season Ayrton Senna won his third and final championship, both with Senna and Gerhard Berger history. The group also includes a 2012 MP4/27A, the 2021 MCL35M that Lando Norris drove onto the podium at Monaco in Gulf livery, and the newest car, the MCL37A, which Brad Pitt drove at the Circuit of the Americas while filming F1. Each car is being offered individually.
